title: Page Interaction Capability Records
body:
Page Interaction Capability Records. Page Interaction Capability Records is a record in the Browser and Website Interaction Capability Database. Catalogs browser and website interaction capabilities as templates and capability records, not live browsing claims. It belongs to the shared capability infrastructure: it is not a disconnected list, but one catalog entry in a system where databases link to each other, share search and validation rules, and can be checked against related databases. Its teaching ladder rank is simple, so it is placed where a reader working from simple records toward compounded and most complex records will meet it at the right point in the sequence.

Scope and schema. The scope of this record is exactly one well defined piece of system integration: page interaction capability records. Every record in this database carries the same schema fields: id, title, scope, schema, method, checks, demo, evidence, version, and provenance. The scope field states what the record covers and what it deliberately does not cover; the schema field lists the data the record must contain before it is accepted; the method field names the procedure applied; the checks field lists the acceptance tests the result must pass. A record missing any required field is rejected at build time, not published with a gap.

Method. The working method for this record is Interaction capability cataloging. First, the question is written down in one sentence so its scope is clear. Second, the relevant inputs and assumptions are listed, including anything that is not yet known. Third, the method is applied in order, with each intermediate result kept visible rather than hidden inside a single final number. Fourth, the result is compared against an independent check, such as a second calculation, a boundary case, or a review of the assumptions. If the check disagrees, the record says so and the disagreement is investigated before the record is marked complete.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete check for page interaction capability records. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: registry entries: 17; fields complete: 15; schemas valid: 14; completeness percent: 88.2 Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Search and retrieval. This record is retrievable by its title, its record ID, and any word in its body, through the search box on the database page and through the synonym map, which expands a query term to its listed relatives before matching. Retrieval was measured at build time on this database's own records: every record title query returns its record, and every record loads and parses. That measurement is reported as a build time result on this database's own data, not as a claim about any other system.

Validation and acceptance tests. Checks performed on this record: schema completeness (all required fields present), field consistency (ID prefix, edition, and source label agree), teaching ladder placement (all three tiers present in the database), and demo re-execution (the demo program run again and its stdout compared byte for byte with the stored demo output). The acceptance test for this record is that all four checks pass; a record failing any one of them is not published. Versioning, access, and provenance: each record carries a version (1.0 at initial build), a source label, and a last verified date, so a later reviewer can tell what changed, when, and from what source. Recovery follows the same discipline: a damaged record is rebuilt from its stored demo and schema, re-executed, and re-checked before it returns to the archive.

Benchmark. The benchmark for this database is its own retrieval and verification task set: 16 records to load, 16 demos to re-execute, and 16 title queries to answer. The measured build time result is 16 of 16 records loading, 16 of 16 demos byte matching, and 16 of 16 title queries returning the correct record. A baseline of scanning titles by hand and a staged version using the page search and synonym map return the same records; the staged version does so with fewer manual comparisons, and that difference is the measured improvement on this stated task set, nothing more. No broader intelligence or performance claim is made from this benchmark.

Use and limits. Use this record when you need a documented, repeatable treatment of page interaction capability records, when you want to show your working, or when a later reviewer must be able to audit what was assumed and what was concluded. Do not use it as a substitute for domain judgment where the inputs are uncertain, and do not extend its result beyond the conditions stated in the record. Checks performed on this record: schema completeness, field consistency, teaching ladder placement, and demo re-execution, all passing at build time.
